title: Retrospective characterization of patients with rare osteological diseases
summary: In Berlin, the care of patients with rare osteological diseases is comparatively well established. With the Department of Osteology at Immanuel Hospital Wannsee, the population of Berlin even has access to an inpatient osteology unit. Outpatient care is also provided. At Endokrinologikum Berlin, patients with rare osteological diseases likewise receive outpatient treatment. Both centers are DVO-certified osteological centers of excellence. Consequently, both centers have a large number of documented cases of various, including rare, osteological diseases, such as pregnancy- and lactation-associated osteoporosis, osteoporosis associated with mastocytosis, and methotrexate-induced osteopathy. Within the framework of this study, we aim to summarize patient and disease characteristics of rare osteological disorders. The published literature is often based on case reports or small case series. We therefore plan a retrospective characterization of patient data. This will include the collection of demographic data, imaging data (characterization of fractures), histological investigations (bone histology), osteodensitometry, laboratory parameters, and medical history (comorbidities and medication), where available.
conditions: pregnancy- and lactation-associated osteoporosis, methotrexate-induced osteopathy, osteoporosis in mastocytosis

interventions.name: Patients from two DVO Osteology Centers of Excellence (Endokrinologikum Berlin and Immanuelkrankenhaus Berlin Wannsee) with one of the following rare osteological diseases: pregnancy- and lactation-associated osteoporosis, methotrexate-induced osteopathy, osteoporosis in mastocytosis

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All adult patients in whom pregnancy-associated osteoporosis, osteoporosis in the context of mastocytosis, or methotrexate-induced osteopathy was diagnosed since the 1990s at Immanuel Hospital Wannsee or at Endokrinologikum will be included in the retrospective data analysis.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria include an uncertain diagnosis or minor age.
